newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. missile inspectors arrive in Baghdad.
newsitem.headline: U.N. missile inspectors arrive in Baghdad.

text.p: A team of United Nations ballistic missile experts arrived in Baghdad on Monday to investigate whether Iraq still had any banned weapons in its arsenal, a U.N. arms official said.
Jo Lomas, special assistant to the director of the Baghdad Ongoing Monitoring and Verification Centre, told Reuters the group comprised eight experts and intended to stay for two weeks.
The team, headed by Charles Besancom of the United States, would meet Iraqi officials and carry out inspections.
The U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) was charged with disarming Iraq under terms of the 1991 Gulf War ceasefire conditions and continues to check for banned missiles which were meant to be destroyed.
"The mission is to verify the number and types of destroyed weapons," Lomas said.
UNSCOM has not yet released results of the analysis of about 100 Iraqi missiles sent for testing in the United States and France in April.
The ceasefire forbids Iraq to keep or produce missiles with a range greater than 150 km (90 miles), or the means to produce such weapons.

UNSCOM must certify that Iraq has no weapons of mass destruction before the United Nations will lift curbs on the country's oil exports, although Baghdad is allowed limited sales under a humanitarian deal.
